Because hazards and vulnerabilities often intersect and are sometimes difficult to isolate (Applegate et al. 2025), this report focuses on risk drivers and provides a qualitative mapping and explanation of the key types of interrelated vulnerabilities affecting DOW’s mission either introduced or exacerbated by the global adoption of advanced energy technologies, highlighting interconnections and nested consequences. Risk drivers are categorized by those originating in (1) energy infrastructure itself; (2) the adoption and integration of advanced energy technologies; and (3) actions of allies, partners, or adversaries. Some of these risks overlap, and mitigation strategies can sometimes simultaneously reduce more than one risk. This report does not address certain concepts outlined in the 2023 U.S. Department of Defense Operational Energy Strategy that are not unique to the adoption of advanced energy technologies. For example, energy demand reduction and the recommendation for enterprise- wide visibility on operational energy supply and demand are not unique to the type of energy generation technology deployed. Such considerations are outside the scope of this analysis.
